prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The GNN partitioner is under-trained at the fixed 100 epochs / lr=1e-3 with a contrastive objective that never sees wirelength, so embeddings are noisy and tier assignment is near-random for large designs; increasing training epochs (100 -> 300) lets the contrastive objective actually separate connected cells, giving a more wirelength-aware partition that shortens both same-tier and cross-tier critical connections and reduces TNS.
Rule-based digest:
total=-0.121 robust(mean-std)=-0.083 min_case=-0.097 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=-0.097 dWNS=-5.2% dTNS=-13.0% overflow~101
  bp-ng45: score=-0.031 dWNS=-6.3% dTNS=-0.8% overflow~125
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.007 dWNS=+6.1% dTNS=-2.7% overflow~150
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis partly held: longer training helped ariane133-ng45 (dTNS -13.0%, dWNS -5.2%) and bp-ng45 (dWNS -6.3%), consistent with better-separated embeddings yielding more wirelength-aware tiers. But bp_fe-ng45 was mixed (dWNS +6.1%, dTNS -2.7%), and all scores are negative overall (total -0.121), so the effect is not robustly beneficial. Overflow ~101-150 suggests congestion may be confounding. Next step: sweep epochs (100/200/300) with a wirelength-aware contrastive term and report per-case WNS/TNS plus overflow, to confirm the mechanism rather than just epoch count.
